operational_definition: An explicit study_id, trial_id, cohort_id, or study_cluster_id field that can group multiple reports
observed_consequence: The retained DOI can identify a report when present, but multiple reports from one underlying study cannot be grouped.

operational_definition: A generic outcome or outcome_measure field
observed_consequence: Most case schemas cannot distinguish estimates for different outcome constructs through a dedicated field.

operational_definition: An explicit follow_up_years, follow_up_months, time_point, or follow_up field
observed_consequence: Estimates measured at different follow-up times cannot generally be separated.

operational_definition: An explicit effect_measure, effect_measure_type, or measure_type field
observed_consequence: No schema has a dedicated effect-measure metadata field; generic effect_size values therefore lack a recorded scale.

operational_definition: An estimate field whose name itself specifies hazard ratio, odds ratio, risk ratio, rate ratio, or mean difference
observed_consequence: One schema names hazard_ratio explicitly; the other nine estimate-and-interval schemas use the generic field effect_size.
Ten schemas collect interval bounds; populated bounds alone do not establish a common estimand or independence.

operational_definition: An explicit variance, within_study_variance, standard_error, or se field
observed_consequence: No schema directly records the within-study variance used for inverse-variance weighting.

operational_definition: An explicit cluster_id, study_cluster_id, arm_id, comparison_id, or effect_id field
observed_consequence: Multiple outcomes, time points, contrasts, and reports cannot be grouped for dependence handling.
